key_cases.holding: The court held that establishing a guardianship under chapter 13.36 RCW by a preponderance of the evidence satisfies due process, because parents retain visitation and modification rights and a guardianship does not sever the parent-child relationship as termination does.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the constitutional standard of proof and the due process analysis governing dependency guardianships in Washington.
key_cases.quote: Since guardianships under the new statute do not rise to the level of terminations, proceedings to establish guardianships do not warrant the same standard of proof as termination proceedings.

key_cases.holding: The court vacated a dependency guardianship and remanded for reinstatement of the dependency, holding that a guardianship may not be imposed where the father had remedied his parental deficiencies so the child could be returned to his care in the near future.
key_cases.relevance: Defines the statutory limits on when a guardianship may substitute for reunification or termination.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that because the father has remedied his parental deficiencies, D.S. can be returned to his father's care in the near future.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: A four-Justice plurality held that Washington's nonparental visitation statute, as applied to order grandparent visitation over the objection of a fit custodial mother without according her decision any material weight, unconstitutionally infringed her Fourteenth Amendment right to make decisions concerning the care, custody and control of her children.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the constitutional limit on transferring custody or visitation rights to relatives over the objection of a fit parent.
key_cases.quote: there is a presumption that fit parents act in the best interests of their children
